text: This is his ninth day one.
And he is about to stop counting.
It started with a mirror.
Tired eyes. Shaking hands. A man he didn't recognize.
Everyone has one thing they keep going back to.
His had been winning for years.
So he hung a calendar on the wall. And drew one small line.
Day one.
Day two. Day three. He felt it working.
Then a bad day at work. And by night, it was over.
He tore the page down.
Day one. Again.
Five days, the next time.
A party. Friends. Come on, just one.
Day one.
Eight days.
A phone call. Bad news. He was alone with it.
Day one.
Eleven days. Nineteen. Twenty-six.
And every time, the same red line through the same small number.
He stopped telling people he was trying.
Saying it out loud only made the falling louder.
And a voice in his head kept score. You always quit. You always will.
Then, his best run yet. Forty days.
He slept through the night.
He laughed again.
Day forty-one... he fell.
That night, he stood in front of the calendar.
Nine attempts. Nine day ones.
He ripped it off the wall.
Why even count?
The torn pages lay on the floor.
And for the first time, he looked at them side by side.
Two days. Three. Five. Eight.
Eleven. Nineteen. Twenty-six. Forty.
Every run... was longer than the one before.
He hadn't been failing. ... He had been climbing.
And every fall had left him something.
Day three taught him: bad days need a plan.
Day five taught him to say no, and leave early.
Day eight taught him to call someone, instead of carrying it alone.
Day forty taught him what his life could feel like.
Day one was never zero.
It was day one, with everything he'd learned.
So he taped the pages back together. And hung a new calendar beside them.
This time, he told a friend.
Day forty-one came. And went.
Fifty. Seventy. One hundred.
The line grew right off the top of the chart.
One morning, the mirror again.
Clear eyes. Steady hands. ... He knew this man.
Maybe he'll fall again someday.
But he will never start from zero.
If today is your day one again...
Starting over is not starting from zero.
Keep going.
